sources.locator: Read in the complete extracted text of the author manuscript: Introduction, §1.1 (commutativity classes), §1.2 (heaps and Proposition 1.2 with the invariance remark), §1.3 (weak order), §2 (Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2, Proposition 2.3), PDF pp. 1-10 (manuscript pp. 1-9). contents.name: Full commutativity: decomposition of R(w) into commutativity classes and the definition of fully commutative elements (§1.1)
Proposition 1.1: w is fully commutative iff no reduced word contains a full alternating braid factor as a contiguous subword
Heap P_s of an arbitrary word as a labeled poset on positions, and linear extensions of a poset (§1.2)
Proposition 1.2: the labeled linear extensions of the heap are exactly the commutativity class
Invariance of the heap under commuting interchanges, and well-definedness of the heap of a fully commutative element (§1.2)
Lemma 2.1: {x : x <=_R w} is isomorphic to the lattice J(P) of order ideals of the heap
Theorem 2.2, implications (a) => (c),(e) and (c),(e) => (b): full commutativity, order-theoretic reduced words and distributivity of the lower interval
Proposition 2.3: a heap is the heap of a fully commutative element iff it has no convex alternating chain of length m(s,t) >= 3 and no covering pair with equal labels
Theorem 2.2, implication (b) => (a): if the lower right weak interval is a distributive lattice then the element is fully commutative
contents.reason: The converse direction is not among the four contracted claims of this pair and no consumer page in the run uses it; its minimal-counterexample and dihedral-weak-order argument is therefore left to a future item rather than scaffolded here.

contents.name: Proposition 1.3 (interval translation) and Proposition 1.4 (the fully commutative elements form a weak-order ideal)
contents.reason: The interval translation is needed only for the unbuilt converse (b) => (a) of Theorem 2.2, and the ideal property is not used by any contracted item; the length-additive facts actually consumed are supplied by the in-run weak-order prefix lemma.

contents.name: §§3-6: maximal quotients, top trees, the FC-finite classification and the Bruhat-order consequences

The owned proofs use Stembridge §1.2 positional dependence, which includes equal labels. See the assigned Step-3b report for the exact source qualification.
